structured_output.hypothesis: If whorl breadths along a radius of spiral gastropod shells form a geometric progression, then log whorl breadth (or log distance from the coiling axis) will be a linear function of whorl number within each shell, with a roughly constant per-whorl ratio.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using the per-shell landmark/whorl-outline measurements of the 176 shells in the dataset, regress ln(whorl breadth at successive whorls along a radius) on whorl number for each shell with at least 4 measurable whorls. The claim passes if the median R^2 of these fits is at least 0.98 and at least 80% of shells have R^2 at least 0.95 (a constant ratio). The Nautilus value (about 3 per whorl, accepted range 2.5 to 3.5) is a separate sub-check, applicable only if Nautilus is in the data.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if the median per-shell R^2 of ln(breadth) against whorl number is below 0.95, or if fewer than 60% of shells reach R^2 of 0.95. It also fails if a quadratic term in whorl number is significant (p < 0.01) in a majority of shells, showing systematic departure from a constant ratio.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'breadth of successive whorls along a radius' is read as the radial width of each whorl, or equivalently the distance from the coiling axis to the whorl outline at successive turns, taken from sagittal-section or apical-view images. A geometric progression means a constant ratio, which is exponential growth with whorl number and a straight line in log space. 'Logarithmic spiral' corresponds to a log-linear fit of radius against whorl angle. This dataset covers gastropods only, with no ammonoids and probably no Nautilus, so the test covers the gastropod part of the claim and not the whole scope. Modern studies use Raup-style or helicospiral parameters, whose expansion rate W is the per-whorl ratio. I have not confirmed which columns the files hold, so the test depends on the landmark .tps file and S_Table_3 containing per-whorl measurements.

dataset.publisher: Dryad (Collins, Klapaukh, Crampton, Gazley, Schipper, Maksimenko, Hines)
dataset.why_it_fits: It holds images of 176 fossil and modern gastropod shells, with landmark data and fitted helicospiral coiling parameters including whorl expansion rate. It can directly test whether whorl dimensions grow geometrically in gastropods. Files include S_Table_1_Specimens.csv, S_Table_3_hangle_output.csv, the Collins_et_al_data.zip archive and R code. The page does not state column names, so I could not confirm that per-whorl widths are recorded. It does not cover Nautilus or ammonoids.

input.pass_criterion: Using the per-shell landmark/whorl-outline measurements of the 176 shells in the dataset, regress ln(whorl breadth at successive whorls along a radius) on whorl number for each shell with at least 4 measurable whorls. The claim passes if the median R^2 of these fits is at least 0.98 and at least 80% of shells have R^2 at least 0.95 (a constant ratio). The Nautilus value is a separate sub-check: a ratio of 2.5 to 3.5 per whorl if Nautilus is in the data.
input.fail_criterion:
The claim fails if the median per-shell R^2 of ln(breadth) against whorl number is below 0.95, or if fewer than 60% of shells reach R^2 of 0.95. Equivalently, it fails if a quadratic term in whorl number is significant (p < 0.01) with its sign and size in a majority of shells, showing systematic departure from a constant ratio.</fail_criterion>
<parameter name="interpretation">Thompson's 'breadth of successive whorls along a radius' is read as the radial width of each whorl, or equivalently the distance from the coiling axis to the whorl outline at successive turns, taken from sagittal-section or apical-view images. A geometric progression means a constant ratio, which is exponential growth with whorl number and a straight line in log space. 'Logarithmic spiral' corresponds to a log-linear fit of radius against whorl angle. The dataset does not cover ammonoids or Nautilus broadly, so this test covers the gastropod part of the claim only. Modern studies use Raup-style or helicospiral parameters, whose expansion rate W is the per-whorl ratio. I have not confirmed which columns the files hold, so the test depends on the landmark .tps file and S_Table_3 containing per-whorl measurements.
